name: turbomachine_optimal_diameter
title: Teaching exercise: optimal diameter and speed of a turbomachine
summary: Teaching exercise on the optimal diameter and rotation speed of a turbomachine. With the flow factor and the enthalpy factor given, the model computes that diameter and speed for air drawn at 1 bar and 20 °C, 6000 m³/h, and discharged at 2.5 bar.

origin.course: ULiège, Machines et systèmes thermiques, repetition 4, exercise 6

verification.summary: Compared with the EES stored solution of MSTh-SB-R4-Ex6.EES using compare_solution.py without --ees-units: 17 common variables, 3 differ (rtol=0.001); only in EES: 0; only in CoolSolve: 1. Those three are h_1, h_3_s and s_su. Maximum relative difference 3.19e-01 on s_su. D_opt, rpm_opt and DELTAh_s stay within rtol=0.001. All 17 equations are satisfied.
verification.reference: EES stored solution of thermo_models TM-0068 (MSTh-SB-R4-Ex6.EES, EES X7.458, 17 variables); tools/compare_solution.py, no unit conversion (already SI Pa, C, J)
verification.notes: The printed maximum is 3.19e-01 on s_su. Unrounded, s_su is the maximum over the 17 common variables at 0.3193992439 (3867.259359 J/kg-K against the EES stored 5682.126158 J/kg-K). h_1 is +125870.58 J/kg and h_3_s is +125897.35 J/kg above the EES values, so the Air enthalpy offset is not constant. That 26.77 J/kg gap is the gap on DELTAh_s (relative difference 3.0378e-04, printed 3.04e-04). D_opt differs by 7.6305e-05 and rpm_opt by 2.2825e-04, both under rtol=0.001. The name present only in CoolSolve is PI. With the .initials file, CoolSolve reports 12 iterations and all 17 equations satisfied (max relative residual 9.1177e-11). Without it, 47 iterations, and D stays positive.
